title: Pakistan: World Liberty deal, Trump-tied lobbyists, minerals and tariffs
summary: Every dated step in the claim is documented: the Seiden/Javelin/Checkmate hires, the 26 Apr 2025 WLF letter of intent (with Munir in attendance), the ceasefire, Munir's lunch, the Nobel nomination, the 19% tariff and oil deal, the USSM $500M minerals MoU, Bin Saqib's regulator admitting Binance and HTX, the 14 Jan 2026 USD1 MoU and the Sep 2026 Powerus order. The second layer adds Rep. Ronny Jackson (via Javelin filings, single-source), a minerals-focused Seiden mandate, and Squire Patton Boggs' 14 May 2025 minerals pitch. What is not substantiated is causation: no source shows the lobbyists arranged the WLF deal, the lunch, the tariff or the Powerus order. Seiden was hired before, not after, the Pahalgam attack.

sub_claims.statement: Timeline anchor: Seiden Law was hired before the Pahalgam attack; Javelin registered and WLF signed its letter of intent within days after it, with Munir in the room.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence: documented. Seiden Law (FARA 7570) signed with Pakistan on 2025-04-08, two weeks BEFORE the 2025-04-22 Pahalgam attack. Javelin Advisors (Keith Schiller, George Sorial) signed a consulting agreement dated 2025-04-24 and registered under FARA (No. 7579) on 2025-04-25, as Seiden's subcontractor. On 2025-04-26 Zach Witkoff, Zak Folkman and Chase Herro signed the WLF letter of intent with the Pakistan Crypto Council in Islamabad. Arab News and Dawn report that the delegation also met PM Shehbaz Sharif, army chief Gen. Asim Munir and Deputy PM Ishaq Dar. Business Today, citing Dawn, says Munir personally attended the closed-door session (secondary). The sequence is documented. That the hires and the letter of intent were coordinated is not reported anywhere (see 'Not connected').

sub_claims.statement: Seiden Law's Pakistan mandate was explicitly about minerals, and it was passed to Trump's former bodyguard's firm.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence: documented (Global Witness analysis of FARA filings; Nukta; Dawn). Global Witness reports that the Seiden contract, $200K/month, was to 'promote the exploration and sale of' rare earths and other critical minerals for Pakistan, and that Seiden outsourced it to Javelin. It names Robert Seiden and George Sorial as Trump-circle figures representing Pakistan. Javelin's share was $50K/month (Politico, Dawn). An unofficial FARA-compilation site says Javelin's engagement ended on 2025-10-08 after four payments totalling $200K. Treat that termination detail as single-source. No 2026 renewal of either contract was found. Audit note: the monthly figure varies by source. Nukta and Global Witness give $200K/month for six months; CAPSS (an Indian think tank) lists $125K/month. The FARA PDFs could not be read directly to settle it.

sub_claims.statement: Javelin's filings put Trump's former White House physician, Rep. Ronny Jackson, in the minerals channel during the India-Pakistan conflict.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence: single-source. The Economic Times reported this from FARA filings by Javelin Advisors and Conscience Point Consulting (another Seiden subcontractor), and Business Today and others relayed it. The underlying filings could not be read directly. Reported details: an in-person meeting between Jackson and Pakistani officials on 2025-05-01 on the rare-earths deal; a 2025-05-28 call followed by an email with a draft MoU, which Javelin's filing describes as 'Delivery of Proposed MoU'; and Javelin contacting Jackson's office during the 7-10 May conflict (ThePrint). Jackson (R-TX) was Trump's White House physician. No comment from Jackson was found. An unofficial site claims a $4,000 contribution to Jackson on 2025-10-28 tied to Javelin. That is unverified against FEC records and is not relied on. Audit (Nov 2026): no response from Jackson or Javelin and no non-Indian outlet independently confirming the filing entries was found, so the grade stays single-source.

sub_claims.statement: During Operation Sindoor, Pakistan's embassy lobbyists pitched a minerals-and-trade partnership to US officials.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence: documented (FARA filings as reported by ThePrint, IANS and others, Jan 2026). Squire Patton Boggs, the embassy's long-standing registrant, sent 50+ emails to Congress and officials between 7 and 10 May 2025, stressing fears that India would resume strikes. On 2025-05-14, four days after the ceasefire, it emailed a US diplomat about a renewed partnership 'centred on trade, especially mines and minerals.' Separately, the embassy hired Ervin Graves Strategy Group in Oct 2025 ($25K/month, three months), partly on keeping Pakistan off the FATF grey list (Business Today), then signed a two-year, ~$1.2M contract with it effective 2026-05-01 ($50K/month) that seeks resumed US-Pakistan defence dialogue and has a section on minerals cooperation (AFP via Arab News/Malay Mail, Dawn). Most of this coverage comes from Indian outlets with an adversarial framing, but it rests on public filings.

sub_claims.statement: Ceasefire -> Nobel nomination -> Munir lunch: Pakistan credited Trump, India did not.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence: documented. Trump announced the ceasefire on Truth Social on 2025-05-10. Pakistan's FM Ishaq Dar confirmed it. India says Pakistan's DGMO initiated it and rejects any US mediation. Trump hosted Munir for lunch on 2025-06-18 (Steve Witkoff present, per C64). On 2025-06-21 Pakistan formally nominated Trump for the Nobel Peace Prize over his 'decisive diplomatic engagement'. Dawn's insiders say the lunch was secured via 'unconventional means', without naming anyone. No source ties any paid lobbyist or WLF figure to arranging the lunch.

sub_claims.statement: Checkmate was paid via a Dubai entity (Greystone) for Pakistan-related government-relations work.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence: the contract is documented; its defence-and-minerals scope is not, and the paying entity's ownership is not established. Checkmate Government Relations (FARA No. 7534; Ches McDowell, a Trump Jr. associate per C64) contracts not with Pakistan's government but with Dubai-based Greystone Investment & Management LLC, from 2025-05-15, with $100K paid on 2025-05-14 for a 30-day Phase I and a $200K Phase II option (O'Dwyer's, FARA exhibits). Its filings describe general government-relations advice and outreach to US officials. Audit correction: the 'two-year, $1.2M agreement covering defence cooperation and minerals' ('support efforts to identify opportunities for cooperation') that Daily Times/AFP describe is Pakistan's embassy contract with Ervin Graves Strategy Group, effective 2026-05-01 at $50K/month for 24 months, not Checkmate's. No coverage found names Greystone's owners or its tie to the Pakistani state. That is a gap, not a finding.

sub_claims.statement: Trade deal, 'massive oil reserves', 19% tariff and a first US crude cargo (Jul 2025).
sub_claims.finding: Evidence: documented. Around 2025-07-30, Trump announced a trade deal and said the US would help develop Pakistan's 'massive oil reserves' (no details). An executive order dated 2025-07-31 set a 19% tariff on Pakistani goods, down from the threatened 29%. Refiner Cnergyico bought a test cargo of about 1M barrels of WTI from Vitol, due in Karachi in the second half of Oct 2025, with possible monthly purchases. No Trump-family or WLF party appears in the oil or tariff steps.

sub_claims.statement: Minerals chain: USSM-FWO $500M MoU, the Oval Office mineral box, the first shipment, the Pasni pitch and EXIM's Reko Diq loan.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence: documented. 2025-09-08: Missouri-based US Strategic Metals (CEO Stacy Hastie) signed a non-binding $500M MoU with the army's Frontier Works Organization at the PM's House, accompanied by the US embassy's acting DCM. 2025-09-26: Munir and Sharif presented Trump with a box of mineral samples in the Oval Office. Early Oct 2025: first consignment (antimony, copper concentrate, Nd/Pr rare earths) shipped to USSM; PTI demanded transparency. ~2025-10-04: the FT reported that Munir's advisers had pitched a US-built minerals port at Pasni (up to $1.2B). A Trump official said it was not discussed; a Pakistani military official said Munir has no official advisers. 2025-12-10: the US announced $1.25B in EXIM financing for Barrick's Reko Diq. No Trump-family stake in USSM, Reko Diq or Pasni was found.

sub_claims.statement: Bin Saqib's regulator opened Pakistan to Binance and Justin Sun's HTX (Dec 2025).
sub_claims.finding: Evidence: documented (Cointelegraph, The News, multiple Pakistani outlets). In Dec 2025 PVARA, chaired by former WLF adviser Bilal Bin Saqib (also PM's Special Assistant on blockchain and crypto), issued no-objection certificates to Binance and HTX, the first step toward licences. This came alongside a Binance MoU to explore tokenising up to $2B of state assets. CZ, pardoned by Trump in Oct 2025 (C09/C36), is a Pakistan Crypto Council adviser and attended. Justin Sun (C05), HTX's adviser, reportedly met Pakistani officials. Bin Saqib said on 2025-12-14 that the NOCs are not a blanket approval. This puts three WLF-linked parties (Bin Saqib, CZ, Sun) on one Pakistani regulatory track.

sub_claims.statement: The 14 Jan 2026 USD1 MoU was signed by Zach Witkoff with the finance minister, witnessed by Sharif and Munir.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence: documented (Dawn, Arab News, Pakistan PID, Decrypt). Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb and Zach Witkoff signed the MoU with SC Financial Technologies LLC on 2026-01-14. PM Sharif and Munir, now Chief of Defence Forces, witnessed it, and the WLF delegation met Munir separately. SC Financial is a Delaware company that co-owns the USD1 brand with WLF, with Zach Witkoff as CEO. The MoU is non-binding: it sets up study of USD1 for cross-border payments and remittances under PVARA oversight, not adoption. Al Jazeera notes that wider USD1 use earns reserve interest for WLF's owners, including the Trump family.

sub_claims.statement: Pakistan's 2026 role as US-Iran broker is tied by reporters to the WLF courtship.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence: the talks are documented; the causal tie is reporters' framing. In Apr 2026 Pakistan hosted or brokered US-Iran talks: Vance led a first round, and Witkoff and Kushner were slated for Islamabad before Trump called the trip off on 2026-04-25 (Fortune). Bloomberg (2026-03-29) attributes Pakistan's standing in 'Trump world' to Bin Saqib's crypto courtship of WLF. He posted a selfie with Zach Witkoff and WLF executives at Mar-a-Lago. Mother Jones says explicitly that it is 'not clear' the WLF relationship is the reason for Pakistan's intermediary role. Steve Witkoff is a WLF co-founder whose son runs it (C14).

sub_claims.statement: Powerus, the Trump sons' drone company, got a Pakistan MoD order the day after meeting Munir (Sep 2026).
sub_claims.finding: Evidence: documented (Reuters via Arab News/Tribune, Dawn/ISPR, Al Jazeera, Defense Post). A Powerus delegation led by co-founder Brett Velicovich met Munir at GHQ Rawalpindi on 2026-09-16. On 2026-09-17 Powerus announced an MoU with the Pakistan Army and a 'limited procurement order' from the Ministry of Defence. Value and systems are undisclosed; ISPR confirmed the meeting, not the deal. At the time Powerus was due to merge with Aureus Greenway, in which Eric Trump and Don Jr. hold an indirect stake via American Ventures (C51/C63); the merger closed around 2026-10-01. Under three months earlier, Powerus had given an Indian manufacturer exclusive rights to its interceptor technology in India (Al Jazeera). A spokesperson said the president has no involvement in Powerus.

sub_claims.statement: Al Jazeera's '$500m for Trump' figure is a Pakistan payment.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence: documented. As relayed in search excerpts (the article itself could not be read directly), the '$500m' in Al Jazeera's 2026-07-03 headline is WLF's 2025 token-sale revenue to the Trump side, not money from Pakistan. Three different '$500M' figures circulate in this story and must not be conflated: the USSM-FWO MoU (Sep 2025), WLF token-sale income, and Aryam/Tahnoon's $500M WLF stake (C06).

corrections: Brief implies all three lobbying hires followed Pahalgam; Seiden Law signed on 2025-04-08, before the 2025-04-22 attack. Only Javelin's registration (24-25 Apr) and the WLF letter of intent (26 Apr) came days after it.
Javelin was Seiden's subcontractor at about $50K/month, not a direct Pakistan contract; Checkmate's counterparty is Dubai-based Greystone, not the Pakistani government.

The Powerus 'order' is a limited procurement order of undisclosed value plus a non-binding MoU; at signing Powerus had not yet completed its merger with the Trump-son-backed Aureus Greenway (closed ~2026-10-01).
Al Jazeera's '$500m for Trump' refers to WLF token-sale revenue, not to any Pakistani payment or to the $500M USSM MoU.
Some coverage calls Ronny Jackson a senator; he is a US Representative (R-TX) and Trump's former White House physician.

Checkmate/Greystone: the two-year, ~$1.2M defence-and-minerals contract is Ervin Graves Strategy Group's (effective 2026-05-01), not Checkmate's; Checkmate's filed engagement is a $100K Phase I with a $200K Phase II option for general government-relations work.
denials_and_context: India denies any US mediation in the May 2025 ceasefire; Pakistan credits Trump.
A senior Trump administration official said the Pasni port proposal was not discussed; a Pakistani military official said Munir has no official advisers.
Pakistani officials stress the Jan 2026 USD1 MoU is non-binding and does not authorise adoption; Bin Saqib says the Binance/HTX NOCs are not blanket approvals.
Powerus spokesperson: the president has no involvement in Powerus; the Trump sons describe themselves as passive investors (C51).
WLF says Bin Saqib's adviser role was unpaid and ended when he joined government (C64).

Mother Jones notes it is 'not clear' the WLF relationship explains Pakistan's Iran-broker role. Pakistan's pivot also has strategic drivers (Iran access, China hedging, minerals) that cut against a purely transactional reading.
FARA registration is a disclosure regime; nothing here shows illegal conduct. No DOJ action on these filings was found.
